text:
Sara (People Ops): FYI — we’re piloting an East Coast Satellite program for folks who want a mix of HQ days + local hub access. Launching May 1. Quick thread for Qs. :tada:

Tom (Finance): What’s the stipend structure? monthly or one-time?

Sara (People Ops): Two parts: a one-time "satellite setup" of $600 for desks/monitors/shipping, plus a $150/mo "hub access" stipend to cover coworking passes or commuter costs.

Jae (Eng Manager): Eligibility scope? remote folks who live on the East Coast only? What if someone commutes from an adjacent state?

Maya (People Ops): Eligibility = Redwood-headquartered employees whose primary homebase is in the defined East Coast region (ME->FL, DC included). Short-term travel/visitor days don’t count. If homebase already outside region, not eligible unless you change your homebase through HR.

Tom (Finance): Quick note on taxes: the monthly stipend is paid as taxable income and will appear on payroll. The one-time setup is a taxable bonus. We’ll handle with normal payroll codes, so people should expect withholding. @Sara we’ll need a headcount file each payroll cut.

Sara (People Ops): Thanks @Tom — will send the roster CSV 5 business days before each payroll cycle for the first 3 months.

Jae (Eng Manager): How do people request the program or change homebase if they want to be eligible?

Sara (People Ops): Fill the Satellite & Homebase change form and indicate expected start date. Link: https://redwoodinference.notion.site/satellite-program-request

people-ops-bot: Form submission received for 3 people from Engineering. (automated)

Maya (People Ops): Important: if you change declared homebase to a different state, that can trigger payroll/state tax nexus and may require benefits/country checks. We’ll route those changes to Payroll and Legal for review. Expect a 7-10 business day review window.

Jae (Eng Manager): If an engineer moves mid-month, is the monthly stipend prorated?

Sara (People Ops): Yes, prorated by calendar days in the month. Example: move effective 15th -> receives (16/30) * stipend. One-time setup is paid after HR confirms the new address and the employee signs the equipment receipt form.

Tom (Finance): Also: if someone keeps homebase in current state but uses the hub occasionally, they’re not eligible. Homebase must be changed for recurring stipend.

Jae (Eng Manager): Shipping equipment — will Redwood cover shipping both ways if they later leave the program?

Maya (People Ops): Redwood covers initial shipping to employee for the setup. If an employee leaves Redwood within 6 months, we may request return of equipment or deduct fair market value as a payroll adjustment (standard policy).

Sara (People Ops): Ops checklist we’ll use (short):
1) Employee files form -> people-ops-bot ack
2) HR verifies address + manager approval
3) Payroll/legal review for tax nexus (7-10 days)
4) Finance schedules stipend/setup payment and roster submission
5) Equipment shipped and receipt signed

Sara (People Ops): For managers: please flag any time-sensitive moves so we can prioritize payroll cutoffs. If you’re unsure about tax risk for a specific county/state, ping Payroll legal with the address.

Jae (Eng Manager): Thanks — can you post a short FAQ in People Ops channel and the Notion page so I can forward to team?

Sara (People Ops): Will do. Draft FAQ + policy posted to Notion by COB tomorrow, will drop link here. :+1:

people-ops-bot: Notion page updated: https://redwoodinference.notion.site/satellite-program-policy (automated)

Tom (Finance): One last ask: tag payroll code "SAT-EC" on the roster CSV so we can reconcile.

Sara (People Ops): Noted — will include SAT-EC. Thanks everyone.

Jae (Eng Manager): Great, appreciate the clarity.

Maya (People Ops): If any edge cases show up (dual-home, short-term remote) escalate to payroll/legal.

Sara (People Ops): Closing thread — any follow-ups, DM me or add to the Notion comments. :wave:
